t: This is the memorial to Frederick Smith, the second Viscount Hambleden, a politician, businessman and hereditary peer who was educated at Eton and New College, Oxford. It is the work of two men who often collaborated. Sir Edwin Lutyens designed it. He is described by the architectural historian Gavin Stamp as surely the greatest British architect of the twentieth century. The sculptor Arthur George Walker made it, and he is also known for his war memorials and for the statue of Florence Nightingale in Waterloo Place.
